# dash-ota

> Self-hosted over-the-air updates for React Native. The CLI signs releases with an Ed25519
> key you hold, the backend only distributes them, and the device verifies against a public
> key compiled into the binary — so a breached backend cannot forge an update.

- [FAQ](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/faq)

## Introduction

- [What is dash-ota?](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/): A self-hosted, security-hardened over-the-air update system for React Native — client, CLI, and backend, all owned by you.
- [dash-ota vs alternatives](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/introduction/comparison): How dash-ota compares to Stallion, hot-updater, CodePush, and expo-updates.
- [Architecture](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/introduction/architecture): How dash-ota's three packages divide trust so no single compromise can forge or apply an update.

## Getting Started

- [If you've never shipped an OTA update](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/getting-started/what-is-an-ota-update): What an over-the-air update is, what it can and cannot change, and the three ideas you need before starting.
- [Prerequisites](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/getting-started/prerequisites)
- [Ship your first update](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/getting-started/quickstart): Backend, keys, app wiring, and a signed update on a real device — start to finish.
- [Concepts & glossary](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/getting-started/concepts): The vocabulary you need — runtimeVersion, bundleVersion, channel, manifest, device key, and more.

## Core Concepts

- [The OTA lifecycle](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/concepts/lifecycle): enroll → check → download → verify → stage → apply → confirm, and the rollback path.
- [Security model](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/concepts/security-model): Where trust lives, what each part of the system can do, and the one boundary worth understanding.
- [Versioning & targeting](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/concepts/versioning-targeting): runtimeVersion, bundleVersion, channels, targetAppVersions, rollout % — and the store-vs-OTA problem.
- [Native vs JS trust split](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/concepts/native-vs-js): Why the trust-critical work runs in native, before and independent of JavaScript.
- [Crash-loop circuit breaker](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/concepts/crash-loop): How a bad bundle auto-reverts so your app always boots to something that runs.
- [Force-update gate](https://scripting-bear.github.io/dash-ota/docs/concepts/force-update): Push users to the store when a native fix is required — the path OTA alone can't cover.
